Article Title: 'Anti-national forces trying to harm India's unity will face consequences': Yogi Adityanath
Article Text:
Anti-national forces harming India's unity will face consequences: Adityanath

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Friday warned that anti-national and anti-social forces seeking to spread hatred or undermine India's unity would face consequences, invoking Lord Krishna's message on the occasion of Janmashtami.Addressing a gathering in Mathura, the birthplace of Lord Krishna, on the second day of his visit, Adityanath emphasised that His teachings and message remained equally relevant today."Wherever the forces of goodness exist, they will be protected under all circumstances. But wherever anti-national and anti-social forces raise their heads, create hatred in society or attempt to harm India's unity, integrity and faith, Lord Krishna had already said 5,000 years ago what their fate would be," PTI quoted the chief minister as saying.Yogi Adityanath also cited the Bhagavad Gita's teaching, "Paritranaya sadhunam, vinashaya cha dushkritam" (for the protection of the righteous and destruction of evil), stressing that it continued to guide society.The chief minister highlighted the Braj region's role in preserving its religious heritage and the memories of Lord Krishna despite repeated invasions and attempts by various groups to impose their faith on India."Many invasions took place and many people tried to impose their faith on India, but no one could erase the Sanatan faith," Yogi Adityanath said."Those who dared to erase Sanatan faith themselves disappeared into the dust, but the memories of Shri Krishna and Radha Rani, not only in Braj but across India, continue to inspire us today and provide an encouraging environment for future generations," he added.The chief minister welcomed devotees arriving in Mathura for Janmashtami and extended his greetings to the people of Uttar Pradesh on the festival marking the birth of Lord Krishna.Yogi Adityanath has been in Mathura since Thursday for Janmashtami celebrations and has been attending programmes ahead of the festival.
Article Summary: Anti-national forces harming india's unity will face consequences: adityanath. Uttar pradesh chief minister says lord krishna's message is equally relevant today. He was speaking in mathura, the birthplace of lord krishna, on the second day of his visit.

Article Title: Air India Phuket-Delhi incident: All 3 hydraulic systems failed; pilot tested positive for psychoactive substance
Article Text:
The hydraulic failure itself, the more immediate cause of the injuries onboard, unfolded within a five-second window. VT-EXO, an eight-year-old A320neo carrying 145 people, had just been cleared to climb from FL340 to FL360 after entering Kolkata Flight Information Region.

MUMBAI: The preliminary investigation into the August 4 Air India Phuket-Delhi accident has found that the aircraft's three hydraulic systems, green, blue and yellow, lost pressure within seconds while the A320 was cruising at 36,000 feet, triggering an autopilot disengagement, stall warning and an altitude upset. Alongside the technical findings, the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has recommended that the DGCA take action against the Pilot-in-Command, who tested non-negative for psychoactive substance use following the flight."The confirmation of use of psycho-active substance is a serious concern, and AAIB recommends appropriate actions by DGCA on priority," the report said. The interim safety recommendation asked the regulator to "take appropriate actions as deemed fit to prevent abuse of psycho-active substance." Post-flight, both pilots underwent a breath analyser test, which came back satisfactory. But the subsequent psychoactive substance detection test returned a non-negative result for the PIC, a finding confirmed by a follow-up laboratory blood test. The co-pilot tested negative on both counts.The hydraulic failure itself, the more immediate cause of the injuries onboard, unfolded within a five-second window.VT-EXO, an eight-year-old A320neo carrying 145 people, had just been cleared to climb from FL340 to FL360 after entering Kolkata Flight Information Region. At 04:02:43 UTC, the flight control system "detected loss of green hydraulic system." Four seconds later, the flight control (F/CTL) system detected loss of Blue and Yellow hydraulic systems. With all three systems compromised simultaneously, the autopilot disengaged, a continuous repetitive chime sounded, and the stall warning triggered for two seconds. The aircraft "encountered altitude upset," gaining 372 feet before falling 292 feet from its assigned level, the report said.The co-pilot, who was Pilot Flying, responded first to the upset before the captain took over the controls. Recovery was swift. "At around 04:02:52 UTC, the Blue hydraulic system was recovered, and a few seconds later, the Yellow hydraulic and the Green hydraulic systems were also recovered," the report said. It restored normal flight control surfaces within seconds of the failure.But with seatbelt signs off during cruise, the sudden upset threw passengers and crew around the cabin. Twenty-four people, including four cabin crew, needed medical attention on landing; four were hospitalised with serious injuries. The cabin damage was extensive: cracked ceiling panels across multiple rows, dislodged overhead bins, a broken emergency exit handle, a lavatory commode "uprooted from its original location," and a bent crew seat. Despite the injuries, the flight crew chose not to divert, opting instead to continue to Delhi while requesting medical priority from ATC. The aircraft landed safely on runway 11L at 05:30 UTC, around ninety minutes after the failure.Investigators have already flagged one detail for closer scrutiny: the aircraft was dispatched from Phuket under an active Minimum Equipment List item for the Power Transfer Unit, invoked a week earlier on July 28. The PTU serves as an auxiliary hydraulic source shared between the green and yellow systems, and its status at the time of the failure is expected to be a focus of the ongoing probe. Flight recorder data has been downloaded and is under analysis, and a technical team from Airbus and France's BEA inspected the aircraft in Delhi in mid-August, after which hydraulic components and fluid samples were removed for further testing.“The Airbus A320 aircraft has three hydraulic systems. They are identified as the green, blue and yellow systems. Together they supply hydraulic power at 3000 psi (206 bar) to the main power users. Services which are not used during flight are isolated from the main supply. Hydraulic fluid cannot be transferred from one system to another. Each system has its own hydraulic reservoir,” the report said, explaining the hydraulics on the aircraft.On the green system, the normal source of pressure is the Engine Driven Pump (EDP) located on the left engine and, as an auxiliary source, the Power Transfer Unit (PTU). On the blue system, the normal source of pressure is the electrical pump (E-Pump) and, as an auxiliary source, the Ram Air Turbine (RAT). On the yellow system, the normal source of pressure is the EDP located on the right engine and as auxiliary sources the PTU and the electric pump (E-Pump). “Each hydraulic system pressurisation information is available for the aircraft systems through one pressure transmitter (numerical value of the pressure), two pressure switches (discrete value indicating if there is a loss of pressure). Relevant Hydraulic components were removed from the aircraft for further analysis,” the report said. The PTU is an auxiliary pressure supply for either the green or yellow systems without transfer of fluid between the two systems. It operates automatically if there is a delta pressure of 500 psi between the green/yellow or yellow/green hydraulic systems, it addedThe said report is preliminary, and a detailed technical investigation is still underway.
Article Summary: Preliminary investigation into the august 4 air india phuket-delhi accident has found that the aircraft's three hydraulic systems, green, blue and yellow, lost pressure within seconds. Autopilot disengaged, a continuous repetitive chime sounded, and the stall warning triggered for two seconds.

Article Title: Former bureaucrat Ashish Joshi questioned by Delhi Police for 9 hours
Article Text:
The matter came to light after Congress leader Sandeep Dikshit, Joshi's friend, posted about it on X

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Former bureaucrat Ashish Joshi was questioned by the Delhi Police Special Cell and was allowed to leave after nine hours on Wednesday, PTI reported.According to sources, Joshi, a former controller of communications in the Department of Telecommunications, had only been called for questioning in connection with an old case. Details of the case were not immediately available.The ex-civil servant was brought to the Special Cell’s office in New Friends Colony around 10 am and released around 7 pm. He was questioned by a team of the Counter Intelligence unit, which recorded his statement."Just got back home. Delhi Special Cell dropped me home. Details later," he posted on X after returning home.In a subsequent post, Joshi claimed he was taken for interrogration under an assurance that it would take "very little time.""However, as the hours stretched on, my repeated requests to inform my wife of my whereabouts, the concerned Police Officials/Officer simply stated they were 'following instructions.' I was only permitted to make a call at 6:38 PM, leaving my family & friends in total panic the entire day," he said, adding that informing a person's family during interrogation or detention is a legal mandate and not an "optional courtesy.The matter came to light after Congress leader Sandeep Dikshit claimed earlier on Wednesday that two Delhi Police personnel had “taken away” Joshi, whom he described as his close friend, from Nehru Park during his morning walk and that his whereabouts were unknown for several hours.According to Dikshit, Joshi, who retired as an additional secretary a few months ago, called him in the morning but he could not answer. When he tried calling back, the phone was switched off.“An eyewitness who was walking with him told the family that two police personnel came and said they had to take Ashish with them for questioning over a recent tweet,” the former MP claimed in a video statement.Dikshit also alleged that lawyers and others sent to the police station were initially unable to get confirmation about Joshi’s whereabouts.A senior police officer, requesting anonymity, maintained that Joshi and his family were duly informed about the case when he was brought in for questioning. He was questioned in a cordial manner and allowed to leave later, the officer added.
Article Summary: Former bureaucrat ashish joshi was questioned by the delhi police special cell. The matter came to light after congress leader sandeep dikshit, joshi's friend, posted about it on x. joshi, a former controller of communications in the department of telecommunications, was only called for questioning in connection with an old case.

Article Title: PM Modi takes stock of flood situation in Varanasi as water crosses warning mark
Article Text:
The Prime Minister directed the district administration to work on a war footing to provide relief to those affected

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday spoke to Varanasi District Magistrate Satyendra Kumar and took stock of the flood situation in the city as the rising water level of the Ganga crossed the warning mark amid incessant rainfall.PM Modi, who is also the Member of Parliament from Varanasi, sought detailed information from the district magistrate about the river's water level and the arrangements being made at relief camps for people affected by the floods.The Prime Minister directed the district administration to work on a war footing to provide relief to those affected and ensure that all necessary facilities are made available immediately.He also instructed officials to make immediate arrangements wherever there is an additional requirement for relief material and expedite relief work for affected people.PM Modi further directed the administration to maintain constant vigilance over the flood situation and relief operations and ensure that immediate assistance reaches those affected.The Prime Minister's intervention came as the Ganga continued to rise in Varanasi.According to the Central Water Commission (CWC), the river's water level reached 70.54 metres at the Rajghat gauge site at 6 am on Thursday, crossing the warning level of 70.262 metres. The water level was rising at a rate of 2 cm per hour.The danger level at the site is 71.262 metres, while the highest flood level is 73.901 metres.The district administration has been closely monitoring areas affected by the rising waters of the Ganga and Varuna rivers. On Tuesday, District Magistrate Satyendra Kumar and Varanasi Police Commissioner Mohit Agrawal inspected several flood-affected areas after travelling by an NDRF boat from Namo Ghat.The officials visited Salarpur, Saraiya, Konia, Pul Kohna, Dhelvaria and Sarai Mohana to assess waterlogging and the situation of residents. They also interacted with affected people and assured them of all possible assistance.The district magistrate directed officials to remain on high alert and keep arrangements ready to shift residents to safer locations. He also ordered that boats and other resources remain available for relief and rescue operations.Relief camps at the Primary School in Salarpur and Vidya Vihar Inter College were also inspected. Officials were directed to ensure adequate food, drinking water, electricity, lighting, sanitation, healthcare and security, with special attention to children, women and elderly people.
Article Summary: Pm narendra modi spoke to varanasi district magistrate satyendra kumar. He took stock of the flood situation in the city as the rising water level of the ganga crossed the warning mark amid incessant rainfall. The prime minister directed the district administration to work on a war footing to provide relief to those affected.

Article Title: To impart nationalistic learning, Bengal to have 1,000 RSS-run schools within a year: Suvendu
Article Text:
Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari set a target Thursday to establish at least 1,000 schools run by RSS

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

KOLKATA: Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari set a target Thursday to establish at least 1,000 schools run by RSS's education wing Vidya Bharati in every district, municipality and panchayat within a year. He also suggested a plan to merge the state's four education departments into one, specifying that there would be no separate administration for madrassa education.Adhikari, who spoke at an event to mark the 74th anniversary of Vidya Bharati at Ramakrishna Mission Institute of Culture, urged the body to shoulder the responsibility of imparting what he termed "nationalistic learning". He invited its brass to the secretariat to meet officials and take the initiative forward.Bengal has 313 such schools. Nationally, Vidya Bharati runs over 12,000 schools and 10,000 Bal Sanskar Kendras. The CM said he wanted the organisation to focus on establishing more schools in Murshidabad and South 24 Parganas, alleging that "more anti-national activities take place" in these districts. The erstwhile TMC govt, he said, polluted the education environment and institutions like Vidya Bharati would need to "help the state come out of this".He accused TMC of even twisting the Bengali syllabus to divide people. "Mother was referred to as 'amma' and not 'ma'... The syllabus was created in such a way that Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar's or Swami Vivekananda's lessons remained neglected..."Invoking Syama Prasad Mookerjee's call of "ek desh, ek bidhan, ek nishan, ek pradhan", the CM said it would apply to education, too. "We won't allow an arrangement where the higher education department will look after all universities, while another department will look after Aliah University," he said. Aliah University is currently managed by the state's minority affairs department. "I felicitated the board toppers. Later, the minority affairs department sent a separate file containing the names of 27 Muslim students. I asked why? ... I have already felicitated 20 students, and they include Muslims, Jains and Buddhists."Anand Rao, a Vidya Bharati official, told TOI its schools train students in "bharatiyatwa (Indianness)" as well as puja rituals. Some run till Class 5, others up to classes 8, 10 and 12.The website of Vidya Bharati Akhil Bhartiya Shiksha Sansthan states its vision is "to develop a system of education which would help build a younger generation committed to Hindutva and infused with patriotic fervour".
Article Summary: Bengal chief minister suvendu adhikari set a target thursday to establish at least 1,000 schools run by rss's education wing vidya bharati. He also suggested a plan to merge the state's four education departments into one, specifying that there would be no separate administration for madrassa education.

Article Title: Chirag Paswan vs Jitan Manjhi in Bihar: SC 'creamy layer' debate divides NDA; will it open up a Pandora's box?
Article Text:
Chirag vs Manjhi: SC ‘creamy layer’ debate puts Bihar NDA unity to test.

Turf war for Dalit leadership in Bihar

Manjhi has accused Chirag Paswan of seeking to maintain 'Dusadh dominance'.

Homogeneous group vs categorisation

Chirag Paswan demanded resignation of Manjhi and his son Santosh Kumar Suman.

Two-fold challenge

'BJP testing people's mood'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Could the open sparring over “quota within quota” between two prominent Dalit faces of Bihar last month open up a Pandora’s box for the BJP-led NDA government? Union ministers Jitan Ram Manjhi and Chirag Paswan engaged in an open war of words last week over a separate sub-category for the most deprived Dalit sections.Manjhi hails from the Musahar community and wants a sub-quota for the marginalised SC communities. Manjhi’s son Santosh Kumar Suman, who is the Bihar minor water resources minister, has demanded a review of the country’s reservation policy to assess which sections have benefited and which have remained deprived even after 79 years of independence. The father-son duo claims they are not against reservations but want either an increase in quota or separate arrangements for sections still deprived of its benefits after seven decades.Chirag Paswan, son of Late Ram Vilas Paswan, objected to calls to introduce the “creamy layer” provision in SC/ST reservations and insisted that those advocating such a move should first resign from their positions. He stressed that the reservation policy was not based on economic status but was designed to address centuries of social discrimination, exclusion and untouchability.This is not the first time the two leaders have openly engaged in a war of words on issues.There have been instances in the past when the two Dalit leaders have openly taken diametrically opposite stands. The latest point of friction was the Bharat Tiwari encounter case of Bhojpur district. While Chirag Paswan vowed to prevail upon Bihar's BJP-led government to ensure that punishment was meted out to all police officials involved in his encounter, Manjhi asserted that police were justified in having opened fire on the 28-year-old man with an "unlicensed" weapon. Tiwari, a self-styled social and political activist, was shot dead following a heated exchange on June 17 when officials of the local administration and police visited his place to interrogate him in connection with incendiary social media posts.Political observers feel the open friction between the two leaders is more of a political fight for Dalit leadership in the state. Analyst Naval Kishore Choudhary, who has observed Bihar politics for decades, says Manjhi and Paswan are engaged in a turf war."The two leaders represent two different constituencies within the SC community and are in race to establish themselves as a bigger leader within the NDA in Bihar. By taking contradictory stands, they are catering to their own constituencies within the community. There perhaps is a tussle between them to prove who is more important for NDA in Bihar," Choudhary said.However, the current issue of their discord, “quota within quota”, is not just contentious but also politically sensitive. The BJP has strategically avoided a debate on the issue of sub-quota within the Dalits, perhaps realising the uncertain fallout of any such debate.A Supreme Court judgment in August 2024, in a 6:1 majority ruling, had allowed states to sub-categorise castes within the Scheduled Castes (SC) based on socio-economic backwardness and degree of under-representation in govt jobs to ensure that the larger pie of 15% SC quota goes to the backwards among them.It had also asked governments to devise suitable criteria to bar the ‘creamy layer’ among SCs and STs from availing reservation. In the process, the SC overruled an earlier judgment of a five-judge bench in EV Chinnaiah case, which had said the SCs were a homogeneous group and could not be sub-categorised.The Modi government had in 2017 constituted a four-member Commission headed by Justice (Retd.) G. Rohini in October 2017 to examine the extent of inequitable distribution of benefits of reservation among the OBCs and to work out the mechanism, criteria, norms and parameters in a scientific approach for sub-categorisation within them. The Commission submitted its report to President Droupadi Murmu on July 21, 2023. However, the report has not been made public yet.Clearly, the government perhaps wants to avoid opening a Pandora’s box. More so at a time when it faces a competing challenge from the upper caste communities also. There were protests against reservations in the national capital last month, and the government engaged with the protesters. On August 21, several people held a protest in the national capital following a call by Reservation Hatao Andolan (Scrap Reservation), an Instagram-based page. The protesters are demanding the scrapping of quotas, saying that economic criteria should be given precedence over caste in determining eligibility for government support and reservation.Later, the representatives of the group held a meeting with Union minister J P Nadda and engaged in a "cordial discussion". "Following the movement that took place at Jantar Mantar on 21 August, cordial discussions were held, as per the pre-determined schedule, with Harsh Dubey, Ran Bahadur Singh Chauhan, and Mrityunjay Pathak, members of the team. In this connection, we will meet again soon," Nadda said in a post on X after the meeting.Nadda's meeting with Reservation Hatao Andolan representatives drew questions from opponents. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke asked Nadda to explain the Modi government's stand on the anti-reservation movement and questioned what Prime Minister Narendra Modi has to say about the August 21 protest. AAP Delhi unit president Saurabh Bharadwaj also sought clarity from Nadda on the government's position, referring to the demand for reconsideration of reservations.These political attacks notwithstanding, the BJP has to keep in mind the upper-caste sentiments. The upper caste vote has largely been with the BJP barring some exceptions, but ahead of the crucial assembly elections in Uttar Pradesh there are reports of discontent in the community.For the BJP, the challenge is two-fold. On the one hand, it has to keep the anti-reservation protesters engaged without enraging the pro-reservation groups. On the other, it has to strike a balance between competing demands of allies on sub-categorisation within the SC community.The BJP already faces pressure from the marginalised groups after stay on University Grants Commission (UGC) rules calling out caste discrimination in universities. The saffron party is also battling opposition allegations that the 2027 caste census deliberately obscures caste data. The 40 questions which are part of the census ask for many personal details, which have not so far been required for any census. However, it does not have a drop-down box for caste, nor does it ask people to self-identify as OBC to allow for proper collation of caste data.Political analyst Uday Chandra says internal conflicts within the SC community is a reality. This is more so in Bihar where Dalit identity is not totally consolidated like in other states. “The “Jati” name takes precedence over the Dalit identity in Bihar and that explains why there is a competing interest between the two Dalit leaders in the state,” Uday Chandra says.“The BJP also faces the challenge of forming new social coalitions in the runup to 2029 Lok Sabha elections. The 2014 and 2019 social coalitions which helped the BJP electorally are starting to fray and may not be effective for electoral gains,” he adds.That perhaps explains why the BJP is treading cautiously and may not be averse to the idea of “quota within quota” like it exits within the OBCs. Nitish Kumar formed the group of EBCs in Bihar and they powered his politics for years.The BJP may also ponder at the prospect of making electoral gains by prioritising the deprived within the Dalits. No wonder, the opposition parties in Bihar are already accusing the BJP of using the two ministers to test people’s mood on the issue.Bihar's leader of the opposition Tejashwi Yadav said: "The BJP is doing all this drama from behind. They are testing people's mood, putting pebbles in the water and seeing what happens." Referring to Majhi and Paswan, he said: "These people are merely characters. They only want posts. They are greedy for positions, chairs, bungalows and security, but have left society behind."Congress MP Pramod Tiwari said Union ministers making allegations against each other "goes against the Constitution". "Perhaps they do not realise that the principle of collective responsibility applies to the Council of Ministers. Whatever a minister says remains the government's position until it is contradicted," he said.But the BJP may not want to make any new experiment now as the very idea is fraught with huge political risks. Hence, to put the sparring Dalit leaders on the back foot, Bihar minister and senior BJP leader Lakhendra Paswan posed a pointed question to both the Union ministers.Without directly endorsing either position, he asked how many people from their respective communities, beyond their immediate families, they had actually helped advance. He reiterated what he described as the BJP’s position on reservation, declaring, “If there is BJP, there is reservation.” BJP national spokesperson Dr Guru Prakash Paswan also reiterated that the government has a clear stand regarding the reservation issue. "Reservation will exist till discrimination exists in society, and our government has strengthened this system. Whatever one says on this can be their personal opinion, but for social justice, the BJP is committed to fulfilling the vows of B.R. Ambedkar," he said.So, while the BJP watches its two allies in Bihar fight, it would hope that the issue does not snowball into a controversy that goes out of hand.
Article Summary: Jitan ram manjhi and chirag paswan engaged in an open war of words last week over a separate sub-category for the most deprived dalit sections. Political observers feel the open friction between the two leaders is more of a political fight for dalit leadership in the state.

Article Title: Nitin Gadkari urges all state governments to allow bike taxis; announces plan for negative points for traffic rule violations
Article Text:
File photo: Union minister Nitin Gadkari

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Union road transport minister Nitin Gadkari Wednesday urged all state govts to allow bike taxis, saying it could give employment to eight crore people.During the launch of a pilot programme — “Suraksha” — for on-the-spot free medical diagnosis and counselling for 10 lakh drivers, construction and high-risk workers involved in building highways and mines, he also said his ministry will amend Motor Vehicles Act to introduce a negative point system for drivers for traffic violations, which will result in suspension and cancellation of driving licence.The initiative will be implemented on 150-km covering Nagpur–Kamptee areas of NH-44 and mining belt in Chandrapur in Maharashtra, with a target of 10,000 people.Speaking about the programme, Gadkari sought better medical tests and healthcare for drivers and construction workers, saying that “health of our drivers is key for road safety and there is a dire need to focus on their eyecare and other health issues they face due to the nature of their work.”On the need to allow private two-wheelers, such as scooters and motorcycles, owners to allow transporting passengers, he said this will create employment opportunities in rural areas. “We have allowed this. But some states are not allowing this. Transport is a state subject. I will urge them to do so as this will give a source of livelihood to many,” Gadkari said.Highlighting the high number of deaths and violations of traffic and transport rules by drivers, the minister said that they have finalised the proposed legislation to penalise the “habitual offenders”. He said, “There will be negative points for each violation and accumulation of a certain point will result in suspension and even cancellation of licences. We hope this will instil responsible driving behaviour,” he said.
Article Summary: Union road transport minister nitin gadkari wednesday urged all state govts to allow bike taxis. He also said his ministry will introduce a negative point system for drivers for traffic violations, which will result in suspension and cancellation of driving licence.

Article Title: 'Why should I even respond to this?': Aaditya Thackeray on Disha Salian case after HC orders CBI probe
Article Text:
Bombay HC orders

CBI probe

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think of the decision to direct the CBI investigation? Supportive Skeptical Neutral 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray on Thursday dismissed allegations linking him to the death of celebrity manager Disha Salian, questioning why he should respond to them. His remarks came after the Bombay high court directed the CBI to probe Salian’s death.Speaking to reporters, Aaditya Thackeray, the son of former Maharashtra chief minister Uddhav Thackeray said, "It's something that I have nothing to do about and not even thought about. Why should I even respond to this? BJP tries to defame everybody. They have tried to make Rahul Gandhi a 'Pappu' for years.”“They have tried to defame me for the last six years. Anybody who pricks the BJP, they have a problem with them. Like I said, when you have nothing to do with anything, why speak on anything or give it any importance? That's my stand..." he added.Earlier in the day, Maharashtra minister Nitesh Rane said that if Thackeray and others named in connection with the case had nothing to do with Salian’s death, they should come forward and clarify their position.Rane said he had maintained from the beginning that Salian’s death should not be treated as a suicide and expressed confidence that the CBI investigation would establish the facts."We were clear from day one that this was not a suicide; this was a murder case.And events of that nature are now coming to light. Now the CBI investigation will begin, and an FIR will be lodged," Rane said.He said he expected the probe to examine allegations of evidence being destroyed and misuse of power."My only expectation is that regarding the wrong that was done to our sister named Disha Salian—the way power was misused to destroy evidence and proof—all of those things are now going to come out. In the end, no matter how much you try to hide the truth, it eventually comes out," he added.The remarks came after the Bombay high court directed the CBI to register an FIR and conduct a thorough investigation into the circumstances surrounding Salian’s death. The court also directed Malvani Police Station to hand over relevant records to the CBI.The high court said no person should be treated as an accused merely on the basis of allegations made before the court.“Nobody shall be treated as an accused unless in the opinion of the investigating officer there are sufficient grounds to raise reasonable suspicion against him depending on the material collected during the investigation,” the court said.The CBI has been asked to appoint a suitably experienced and senior officer to conduct the investigation.The court also said that if the probe finds that no criminal case has been made out, the CBI must file an appropriate summary report before the competent court.“In case the investigation reveals that no case is made out, then the CBI shall file the appropriate summary report before the court concerned,” it said.Salian’s father, Satish Salian, would be free to challenge such a report and file objections before the court.The high court had earlier raised concerns over the registration of only an Accidental Death Report (ADR), instead of an FIR, despite allegations made by Salian’s family. It also noted that copies of the post-mortem report and ADR had not been provided to the family even years after her death.Advocate Nilesh Ojha, who represented Satish Salian, said the court had directed the CBI to record his statement and appoint a senior officer to investigate the case.The court described Salian’s father as an “unfortunate” parent who had lost his young daughter in “tragic circumstances” and said the matter required a substantive investigation. However, it did not make any adverse finding against any individual named in the allegations.Thackeray had separately approached the high court seeking to intervene in the proceedings. In his application, he described Satish Salian’s petition as “false, frivolous and motivated” and sought an opportunity to be heard before any order was passed.Salian, a celebrity manager, was found dead on June 8, 2020, after falling from a building in Mumbai. Her death occurred days before actor Sushant Singh Rajput was found dead at his Bandra residence.
Article Summary: Bombay hc orders cbi probe into death of celebrity manager disha salian. Shiv sena leader aaditya thackeray dismisses allegations linking him to the death. Maharashtra minister nitesh rane says thackerays should come forward and clarify their position. Thackeray had separately approached the high court seeking to intervene in the proceedings.

Article Title: Nepal floods bring 'unusual' fish to Bihar, govt warns people not to eat or sell them

BETTIAH: Unidentified and unusual fish swept into the Gandak river and its floodplains by floodwaters from Nepal have prompted the Bihar govt to issue a safety advisory, asking residents of West Champaran and Gopalganj not to consume or trade in such fish until their identity and safety are confirmed.The fisheries division of the dairy, fisheries and animal resources department issued the caution on Tuesday after unusual fish were found in local water bodies and low-lying areas across the flood-hit Gandak basin.Floodwaters from Nepal have entered the Gandak system, inundating several areas of West Champaran and Gopalganj. The department said fish can be swept away from ponds, rivers and other water bodies during floods and carried over considerable distances. During this movement, they may come into contact with contaminated drains, dead animals and other pollutants, raising the risk of contamination by bacteria, viruses and fungi.“Do not consume any unidentified or unusual-looking fish. Until confirmation by the concerned department, an unfamiliar fish should not be considered fit for consumption,” the advisory said.Residents have also been asked not to buy or sell unfamiliar fish caught from floodwaters or assume an unusual-looking species is safe merely because it resembles a commonly eaten fish.Anyone developing vomiting, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, dizziness or breathing difficulty after consuming such fish has been advised to seek immediate medical attention.Wildlife Trust of India director Sameer Kumar Sinha said most fish swept into the Gandak in Bihar following the Nepal floods are believed to be ‘Bagarius bagarius’, commonly known as the goonch catfish and locally called “Gochita”.He said the large freshwater catfish is found in fast-flowing rivers of India, Nepal and parts of Southeast Asia. The carnivorous species feeds on smaller fish, crabs and other aquatic organisms and often hides among rocks in deep stretches with strong currents.Sinha said local communities consume the fish, but it spoils quickly after death and may pose health risks if eaten after deterioration. He urged people to follow the Bihar govt advisory and exercise caution. The species is listed by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) as threatened.

NEW DELHI: In a fresh push to curb vehicular pollution, govt will soon allow old polluting trucks and buses to be fitted with retrofit emission-control devices (RECDs) that can reduce particulate matter emissions by up to 90% and nitrogen oxide emissions by 60%. Road transport minister Nitin Gadkari announced the measure Thursday, a move that will complement govt's scrappage and replacement programme for ageing heavy vehicles.Speaking at an event organised by Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (Siam), Gadkari said the device, developed from an innovation at IIT-Delhi, has been successfully tested. Once retrofitted in BS-IV, BS-III and older diesel vehicles, it can bring their emissions on a par with BS-VI standards. Similar devices have already been installed in diesel generator sets to reduce pollution. Gadkari said each device is expected to cost around Rs 4,000-5,000.TOI has learnt that to enable the rollout, road transport ministry will soon notify Automotive Industry Standard 228, which will prescribe technical requirements and performance standards for these devices.Gadkari also highlighted India's acute shortage of buses, saying the country has only two buses per 1,000 people, compared with the global benchmark of eight.He stressed the need for innovative public transport solutions in Tier-II, Tier-III and smaller cities, arguing that metro rail projects are often too capital-intensive to be viable in such places.Taking a swipe at bureaucratic resistance, Gadkari referred to the proposed flash-charging articulated bus system in Nagpur and said, "IAS officers think they are the only intelligent people in the country. Politicians may know only how to win elections, but they believe only they have knowledge.They keep creating hurdles, but it is my responsibility to resolve them."Gadkari also reiterated his ministry's plan to introduce a negative points system for traffic violations to crack down on habitual offenders. The proposal, which he announced Wednesday while launching the 'Suraksha' pilot programme for on-the-spot medical diagnosis and counselling of 10 lakh drivers, construction workers and other high-risk workers involved in highway and mining projects, will assign penalty points for every traffic violation. Drivers accumulating points beyond a specified threshold could face suspension or cancellation of their driving licences, he said.
Article Summary: Govt will soon allow old polluting trucks and buses to be fitted with retrofit emission-control devices. Road transport minister nitin gadkari announced the measure thursday. He said the device, developed from an innovation at iit-delhi, has been successfully tested.

Article Title: SC: BCI writ runs only over lawyers, not law students
Article Text:
Supreme Court Thursday ruled that Bar Council of India has no jurisdiction to discipline or regulate law students

Only parent institution can take disciplinary action, says SC

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Thursday ruled that Bar Council of India has no jurisdiction to discipline or regulate law students and quashed its letters threatening to debar Nalsar University law graduates from registering as advocates for opposing an invitation to CJI Surya Kant as chief guest at the institute's annual convocation.Despite BCI chairperson Manan Kumar Mishra pleading for closure of the issue saying that the objectionable letters to the Hyderabad institute on Aug 13 were withdrawn within hours, a bench of CJI Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said the ambit of BCI's powers, as the statutory regulatory body for the legal profession, is required to be delineated."From an in-depth consideration of the issue, we are of the opinion that Advocates Act, 1961, whereunder BCI is statutorily created, does not confer any express or implied power on BCI or state bar councils to take any disciplinary or punitive action against law students. BCI has disciplinary jurisdiction over law graduates only after they have registered as advocates," SC said.The bench agreed with senior advocate K Parameshwar who, for former Nalsar law graduate petitioners, argued that BCI does not have jurisdiction over law students, and its Aug 13 letters amounted to making deep inroads into freedom of speech and expression of students.So far as law students are concerned, it is the parent institution or the authority prescribed under laws and bylaws governing the institution who alone have the competence to take disciplinary action, if so required, against the students,” said the bench.Parameshwar said while the letter threatened to bar the registration of the Nalsar 2026 batch of law graduates as advocates, a second letter, while withdrawing the threat, directed the university to identify the students who had given the call to oppose the invitation to CJI as chief guest at the convocation. The advocate added that both letters were without jurisdiction.On Aug 14, SC stayed the operation of both letters, terming them “absolutely uncalled for”, and shielded the students and faculty ag-ainst any action by the university pursuant to BCI’s letters.BCI chief Mishra said that both letters were withdrawn subsequently.The CJI-led bench said, “Having held so, we declare all the communications of Aug 13 or subsequent modified communications to be wi-thout any authority of law.”This indictment and clipping of wings of BCI come a day after the same bench entertained petitions alleging serious irregularities in its functioning and its composition without proper elections.On Aug 14, the bench had also said BCI had nothing to do with the students’ protest against the invitation to CJI. “The students might have written a letter to me. It is a dialogue between me and students. Who are they (BCI) to unnecessarily create an issue? This action is totally uncalled for,” CJI had said.Trashing BCI’s threat, CJI had told Parameshwar to convey to the students “to get licences to practice at the earliest and begin their careers in Supreme Court. We will empanel them and give them legal aid cases. This will be our response to all those who intend to create impediments in their professional career.”
Article Summary: Supreme court thursday ruled that bar council of india has no jurisdiction to discipline or regulate law students. Only parent institution can take disciplinary action, says sc. Bci has disciplinary jurisdiction over law graduates only after they have registered as advocates, sc said.

NEW DELHI: National Human Rights Commission has issued notices to the ministries of electronics and information technology (MeitY) and information and broadcasting (I&B) as part of the ongoing scrutiny of circulation of child sexual abuse material on Instagram NHRC member Priyank Kanoongo, whose bench issued the notices on Sept 2, highlighted that the inquiry was no longer confined to who uploaded objectionable content on a platform. "It also examines the extent to which the platform's own editorial and publishing systems participate in the generation, selection, circulation, amplification or monetisation of content," he said.The bench has asked whether a digital platform's legal position can continue to be treated merely as that of a passive intermediary when its systems actively generate, modify, curate, recommend, publish, amplify or monetise content.The commission has specifically asked the I&B ministry whether Meta falls within its regulatory purview as a publisher or publisher of online curated content under IT Rules, 2021 wherever the company's systems generate, modify, curate, recommend, publish or amplify content.Meta owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp.Details have also been sought regarding the regulatory status and obligations of Meta and the action required to be taken by the ministry under the existing regulatory framework.The notices to the minis-tries follow ones issued to Delhi Police in July after NHRC took cognisance of allegations concerning paid ads on Instagram that facilitated access to child sexual abuse material. The commission has now sought action taken reports within two weeks from MeitY and the I&B ministry.The matter arose after media reports by BBC World Service alleged that paid advertisements using terms such as "rape video" and "child video" were being displayed on Instagram to redirect users to Telegram channels where such material was allegedly offered for sale.The bench has also sought a response from MeitY regarding compliance with the provision on mandatory reporting of offences under Pocso Act 2012 and on whether the matter was reported to the special juvenile police unit or the local police. If not, MeitY has been asked to identify the officer or authority responsible and indicate the action taken for the lapse.Material placed before NHRC includes screenshots of Meta's systems which, according to the complainant, provide suggestions relating to content ideas, audience engagement strategies and monetisation methods.
Article Summary: National human rights commission has issued notices to the ministries of electronics and information technology (meity) and information and broadcasting (i&b) nhrc member priyank kanoongo, whose bench issued the notices on sept 2, highlighted that the inquiry was no longer confined to who uploaded objectionable content.

Article Title: Poverty, inequality seed delinquency in minors: SC
Article Text:
The order stands in stark contrast to the lengthy judgement by a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and Ujjal Bhuyan on July 21

NEW DELHI: The full benefit of protective provisions of Juvenile Justice Act has not yet been extended to children who generally develop delinquent behaviour due to having grown up in poverty and environs marked by inequality, illiteracy and discrimination, Supreme Court has said.Exonerating a minor from the charge of attempt to erase evidence in a dowry death case, a bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Sh-ree Chandrashekhar traced in detail the history and development of JJ Act. They said because of industrialisation and urbanisation, rural folk migrated to cities and this weakened community cohesion, resulting in families losing control over their children.Writing the judgement, Justice Chandrashekhar said Wednesday, "Poverty, inequality, illiteracy and the discriminatory environment in which a child grows trigger delinquent behaviour... The rise in the number of cases coming to this court raising the plea of juvenility for the first time indicates in ample measure that there is a huge gap in understanding of the law by stakeholders."The order stands in stark contrast to the lengthy judgement by a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and Ujjal Bhuyan on July 21 in the case 'X vs Bihar' where they held "today's children are exposed to complex information, graphic content and adult experience that were inaccessible to the previous generation".Writing the July 21 judgement, Justice Pardiwala had analysed what propelled a person to commit a crime - "It could be enmity, it could be poverty, it could be greed, it could be perversity in mind and many others..." But the bench had not mentioned inequality, illiteracy, or a discriminatory environment as grounds for a child to turn delinquent.The bench had further said, "There is no doubt that proliferation of technology and the pervasive influence of social media has altered the cognitive and psychological development of children. In such circumstances, courts as living institutions must be responsive to this reality.""The approach of courts or the juvenile justice boards dealing with a child in conflict with the law cannot remain stagnant since the legislation came to be enacted. It must bear a balanced approach towards the evolving nature of the juvenile and legitimate demands of society," Justices Pardiwala and Bhuyan had further said.Justices Mishra and Chandrashekhar said the prosecution's eagerness to bring the culprit to court and forgetting to assess the boy's age led to overlooking of JJ Act and violation of the rights of juveniles in conflict with the law."A child should not be treated as a criminal. He is a victim of the circumstances. Sometimes he is drawn to a world of crime due to socio-economic or emotional and psychological reasons. The state owes a responsibility to reintegrate juveniles in society, rather than permanently stigmatising them," Justice Chandrashekhar said.
Article Summary: The full benefit of protective provisions of juvenile justice act has not yet been extended to children who generally develop delinquent behaviour, supreme court says. The order stands in stark contrast to the lengthy judgement by a bench of justices j b pardiwala and ujjal bhuyan on july 21.

Article Title: Council can seek appraisals from teachers' institues: SC
Article Text:
Supreme Court Thursday underscored the importance of the quality of teachers

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Thursday underscored the importance of the quality of teachers, who play a vital role in shaping the future of the country, and held National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE) can seek annual performance appraisal report (PAR) from teacher education institutions (TEIs).A bench of Justices P S Narasimha and Alok Aradhe said the role of NCTE in ensuring quality education for children is immense and teacher education has assumed greater importance since right to education has been recognised as a fundamental right under Right to Education Act.The bench stressed that it is necessary for the council and its bodies to ensure accountability of educational institutions. It quashed the HC order which had found fault with the council's decision to seek PAR from TEIs. "We fail to understand how a regulatory measure of a statutory body, empowered to achieve planned and coordinated development of teacher education system in the country, could be restrained from calling upon TEIs to file PAR. ...it is but natural and incidental that NCTE would require the stakeholders to provide the necessary PAR," it said.

Justices p s narasimha and alok aradhe said the role of ncte in ensuring quality education for children is immense. The bench stressed that it is necessary for the council and its bodies to ensure accountability of educational institutions.

SRINAGAR: All seven districts of Ladakh will now have autonomous hill development councils, with lieutenant governor Vinai Kumar Saxena approving a notification to this effect Thursday. The move paves the way for local self-governance in all seven districts of the UT through the councils, elections to which will be held soon.So far, only Leh and Kargil districts had Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Councils (LAHDCs). On July 13, the central govt announced the creation of LAHDCs for Sham, Nubra, Changthang, Zanskar and Drass districts, too. The UT administration had notified the creation of the five new districts in April this year.“The framework of elected local self-governance, which was limited to Leh and Kargil, will thereby be also extended to the five newly created districts in the UT,” a govt spokesperson said.The elections to the newly constituted councils will be held in due course after a formal notification is issued under section 8 of the LAHDC Act, 1997, the spokesperson said, adding that the notification would come into force from the date of its publication in the Official Gazette.The LAHDC-Leh was established under the LAHDC Act, 1995, while the LAHDC-Kargil was set up in 2003. Elections for both the councils are held every five years.Currently, only the LAHDC-Kargil has an elected body, as elections to its counterpart in Leh could not be held following the Sept 24 violence last year, when four people were killed after the police allegedly opened fire on protesters demanding Sixth Schedule protections and statehood for the region.In a statement here, Saxena thanked PM Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah for the historic step, stating that the establishment of the seven councils was a milestone in strengthening grassroots governance in Ladakh, allowing local aspirations and priorities to be reflected more effectively in district-level planning and development.
Article Summary: All seven districts of ladakh will now have autonomous hill development councils. The move paves the way for local self-governance in all seven districts. So far, only leh and kargil districts had ladakh autonomous hill development councils.

Article Title: CEA proposes mandatory storage for solar, wind projects
Article Text:
Govt proposes phased storage mandate for new solar, wind projects from 2027, starting at 10% capacity with two-hour duration. (AI-generated image)

NEW DELHI: New solar and wind power projects may have to install battery storage alongside generation capacity from 2027, with govt proposing a phased storage requirement as part of revised technical standards for renewable energy plants.Under the draft regulations issued by the Central Electricity Authority (CEA) on Thursday, ground-mounted solar and onshore wind projects commissioned after July 1, 2027 will have to install co-located energy storage equivalent to at least 10% of their installed capacity, with a minimum storage duration of two hours.This means a 100 MW solar plant would need at least 10 MW of storage capacity capable of storing electricity for two hours, or 20 MWh.The requirement will become more stringent for projects commissioned after July 1, 2029 and up to June 30, 2031. Such projects will have to provide storage equivalent to 10% of installed capacity but with a minimum duration of four hours. A 100 MW plant would therefore require 10 MW/40 MWh of storage.The move comes as the share of renewable energy in the power mix rises and the grid increasingly has to manage fluctuations in solar and wind generation.While there is abundant renewable generation during solar hours, it can lead to curtailment due to insufficient evacuation capacity. Storage will allow surplus electricity to be stored and used during non-solar hours.More than 8,133 gigawatt-hour (GWh) of solar energy - equivalent to 1.5 days of the entire country's total power consumption or enough to power nearly 1.4 million homes for an entire year - was curtailed during the first quarter of the ongoing financial year as the grid could not absorb excess supply during daytime. “Large-scale deployment of battery energy storage systems and grid-forming inverters are crucial for integrating renewable energy into the grid,” said a new and renewable energy ministry official.The CEA has also proposed that renewable energy plants commissioned after July 1, 2027 have at least 15% of their inverters equipped with grid-forming control. All power conversion systems of battery energy storage systems will also have to have grid-forming capability.Grid-forming technology allows power electronic equipment to help establish and maintain grid voltage and frequency, which becomes increasingly important as the share of inverter-based renewable generation rises.Stakeholders have been asked to submit suggestions on the draft Central Electricity Authority (Technical Standards for Construction of Electric Plants and Electric Lines) 2nd Amendment Regulations, 2026 by Oct 4.
Article Summary: Govt proposes phased storage mandate for new solar, wind projects from 2027, starting at 10% capacity with two-hour duration. Move comes as the share of renewable energy in the power mix rises and the grid increasingly has to manage fluctuations in solar and wind generation.
